images.name: porkbot/api
images.reason: Measured 721 MiB on the alpine runtime base (804 MiB on the bookworm base it replaced). The headroom is one large dependency's worth: the budget is under the old base's size on purpose, so reverting the runtime base fails here rather than silently re-inflating every service.

images.name: porkbot/migrate
images.reason: Measured 721 MiB — it carries the same deployed workspace as the api, so it shares the api's ceiling and the same under-the-old-base property (804 MiB before).

images.name: porkbot/worker
images.reason: Measured 517 MiB on the alpine runtime base (600 MiB before). The headroom is one large dependency's worth, and the ceiling is under the old base's size so a reversion cannot pass unnoticed.

images.name: porkbot/backup
images.reason: Measured 477 MiB now that the image is the Node runtime plus the two Postgres clients (1014 MiB when it carried the whole server image for them). The ceiling is far under the old shape, so a return to a server base is a red budget rather than a slow drift.

images.name: porkbot/supervisor
images.reason: Measured 436 MiB on the alpine runtime base (520 MiB before). Same headroom as its siblings: enough for one dependency, not for a toolchain.

images.name: porkbot/proxy
images.reason: Measured 87 MiB: the pinned Caddy image plus the built SPA in /srv/client. The margin is the client bundle's growth, and it is deliberately tight — the proxy must never come to carry a Node runtime.
